source_read: PDF pp. 1365-1368 (PDFs/MDMA/Parrott_2011_ReinterpretationOfHalpern.pdf): the letter (pp. 1365-1367, nine running-text paragraphs, 25 references) read in full; the Fisk et al. letter beginning on p. 1368 read only far enough to separate it. Numbers and quotations attributed to Halpern et al. (2011) checked against PMC3053129 (Tables 1-4, Results, Discussion).

design.note: A letter to the editor with no data; the schema has no 'letter' value, so narrative-review with the design_detail spelling out what it is, is the workable choice. The detail that the 'Declarations of interest: None' on p. 1368 belongs to the following letter is right.

instrument.note: none-applicable (editors' narrative-review checklist), as for any commentary or letter under METHODS §5.3.

key_findings.note: p. 1365, 2nd paragraph: P=0.017, P<0.001 over 27 published studies, six of seven variables, NART IQ the exception.
p. 1365, 4th paragraph: the four factors, the below-50-occasions statement with the page reference to the author's 2006 review (pp. 148-149), and Halpern's median of 43.5.

Medians of 10 alcohol intoxications, 10 cannabis intoxications and 0 cigarettes a day (IQR 0-0.3) are as printed. I also confirmed the card's cross-check in Halpern's Table 1: alcohol intoxications median 10 in both groups, marijuana intoxications median 10 against 1.
The five tests and p values match Halpern's Table 2 (0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.05, 0.02), and Raven's Progressive Matrices at p=0.05 is indeed not listed.
P=0.02 whole group, P=0.003 heavier subgroup, dominant hand unimpaired, Halpern's 'probably chance' reading, all at p. 1366, 7th paragraph.
Median 121 days is also Halpern's Table 1 value.

reporting_issues.note: Halpern's Discussion reads 'More likely, such differences represent chance associations' and 'Exploratory analyses suggest that even the more robust difference on the grooved pegboard ... was likely due to chance'; the letter prints 'More probably ... report' and 'due probably to chance'.

Halpern's Results, 2nd paragraph lists the lower vocabulary score among the group's characteristics, and the Discussion, 1st paragraph attributes it to premorbid ability; the letter counts it among the drug-related impairments.
The source prints exact p values; the letter prints inequalities. Digits backwards and Raven's both stand at p=0.05 in Table 2, and only the first is listed.
The 2013 review's description (p. 7-8 of the in-press proof) and this letter's description of the same tables disagree, and the letter is the one that matches Halpern's Tables 2 and 3.

domains.note: some-concerns is fair: the frame is the author's own model and two of the supporting studies are his, but most of the cited imaging work is other groups'.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial. The letter's own numbers (uncorrected p values between 0.01 and 0.05, subgroups that do not differ, one difference on a premorbid measure) do not carry its conclusion that MDMA is 'cognitively damaging'.

missed: p. 1366: the letter infers from two medians (98 lifetime raves, 43.5 lifetime ecstasy occasions) that 'for the majority of raves visits they were not on ecstasy'. Medians of two different distributions cannot be subtracted in this way for individuals, and the inference carries the letter's argument that this sample was at the careful end of the spectrum. This belongs in the reporting issues.

p. 1366: the letter gives Halpern's subgroup definition as 'moderate users defined as fewer than 50 life-time occasions'. Halpern's moderate group is 17-50 episodes (17 was an entry criterion), so the letter's phrasing drops the floor of the range.

p. 1366: the 800% cortisol increase used to argue that this sample was protected is a measurement in dance-clubbers from the author's own study (its reference 6), not a measurement in Halpern's participants.

The letter never mentions Halpern's equivalence analysis (its Table 4), which is that study's quantitative answer to how large an effect could be ruled out. A letter arguing that real deficits are present should be recorded as having left the study's own precision estimate out.
